messages.content: Explain how chat are opened in the right side of the board

I'll dig into the involved pieces before explaining, so the answer matches the real code paths.## TL;DR The right-side chat is **not** a global "chat panel" — it is an *inline detail pane* owned by `KanbanBoardView.vue`. Clicking a card on the canvas sets `sideTaskId`, a `computed` resolves the live chat record from the chats store, and that record is rendered by `` inside the **right slot** of a `VerticalSplitter`. On mobile (no room, no splitter) the same click instead delegates to the *global* chat opener (`$chats.setActiveChat` → dockview panel / route). So there are **two independent mechanisms** that both end up showing a chat: | Mechanism | Trigger | Where it renders | State owner | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Inline pane** (right side) | Card click on desktop | `VerticalSplitter` `#right` inside the board | `sideTaskId` (local to `KanbanBoardView`) | | **Global chat app** | Ctrl/Cmd+click, ↗ button, mobile tap, Wall card, `setActiveChat` anywhere | dockview panel (`desktop` route) or `/chat/:id` route | `$storex.chats.activeChatId` + `$storex.ui.openApps` | --- ## 1. The entry point: `onSelectTask` Both board flavours funnel into the same handler: `SprintBoardCanvas` emits `@open-task`, and `SprintBoardView` re-emits it up to `KanbanBoardView` (`@open-task="onSelectTask"` in *both* the kanban and the sprint branch). ```js src/components/kanban/board/KanbanBoardView.vue onSelectTask(task) { if (!task) { this.selectedTaskId = null this.sideTaskId = null return } // Card already shown in the pane → toggle it closed if (this.sideTaskId === task.id) { this.selectedTaskId = null this.sideTaskId = null return } this.selectedTaskId = task.id if (this.isMobile) { this.$chats.setActiveChat(task) return } this.sideTaskId = task.id // Make sure the full history is loaded before ChatView renders it this.$storex.chats.loadUninitialized(task) } ``` Three deliberate separations here: - **`selectedTaskId`** = visual highlight on the canvas card. - **`sideTaskId`** = whether the right pane is open, and *which* chat it shows. - **Toggling**: clicking the already-open card closes the pane instead of re-opening it (cheap "peek" interaction, no explicit close needed). --- ## 2. The pane's content source: a `computed` over the store ```js src/components/kanban/board/KanbanBoardView.vue // Chat record shown in the inline detail pane (null hides the pane) sideTask() { if (!this.sideTaskId) return null return (this.$storex.chats.chats || {})[this.sideTaskId] || null } ``` This is the key design decision: the pane renders **the live store object**, never a copy. Streaming (`$storex.chats.onChatEvent`) mutates `state.chats[id].messages` in place, so tokens, tool calls and status changes appear in the pane without any re-fetch and without remounting `ChatView`. > `null` here is also the "pane closed" signal — the whole right slot disappears (see §3), so there is no dead empty panel. `loadUninitialized(task)` matters because board lists/`search` register **summaries** (last message only, flagged `needsReload`). Without it the pane would open on a truncated history until the next socket event. --- ## 3. The layout: `VerticalSplitter` ```vue src/components/kanban/board/KanbanBoardView.vue ``` ```js boardSplitterPanels() { return { left: { defaultSize: this.sideTask ? 60 : 100, minSize: 30 }, right: { defaultSize: 40, minSize: 25 } } } ``` How the split behaves: | Situation | Result | | :--- | :--- | | No task open | `boardSplitterPanels.left.defaultSize = 100`, and the `#right` template is absent → `$slots.right` is `undefined` → `VerticalSplitter` renders **no** second `SplitterPanel` and **no** resize handle. Board is full width. | | Task open (desktop) | Right panel mounts at `40%`, `minSize: 25`, handle becomes a visible grip (`showHandle`) so the divider is discoverable. User drag keeps ~60/40. | | Mobile | `:split="!isMobile"` → `VerticalSplitter` falls back to a plain flex container, and `v-if="sideTask && !isMobile"` means the pane **never** renders. | Inside `VerticalSplitter`, `onLayout` only records the size while **both** slots are present, so closing the pane doesn't wipe the remembered split — it reappears at the width the user last chose when the next task is opened. --- ## 4. What the right slot actually contains ```vue src/components/kanban/board/KanbanBoardView.vue ``` - **`:key="sideTask.id"`** forces a *fresh* `ChatView` per task. `ChatView` keeps internal state (`activeChatId`, `showLogs`, `showHistoryWall`, `compactSidebar`, scroll position) — without the key those would leak from one task to the next. - **`@chats="closeSideTask"`** is `ChatView`'s "navigate away from the chat" event (emitted by `onBack` / delete when there is no parent). Closing the pane is the correct inline interpretation. - **`ChatIcon`** reuses the shared mode icon map (task/chat/code/prview/…) so the pane header communicates *what kind* of chat is open. ### What `ChatView` does when it mounts `ChatView` is not a pure presentational component — it is self-sufficient: ```js ChatView.vue (created → init) await this.$service.chat.findChat(sourceChat) // locate the chat in the right project API if (!this.theChat) await this.$chats.loadChat(sourceChat) this.setProjectContext() if (!this.$storex.projects.kanban) await this.$storex.projects.loadKanban() await this.loadHierarchy() // parents + children (subtasks) await this.loadChatProfiles() ``` and `theChat` always re-resolves through the store: ```js theChat() { const chatId = this.activeChatId || this.chat?.id || this.params?.params?.chat?.id return this.$chats.chats[chatId] || null } ``` So the board pane gets the **whole** chat surface for free: header, breadcrumb, subtask sidebar (collapsed by default via `compactSidebar: true`), logs, timeline, export, settings. The board does not duplicate any chat logic — it only owns *placement*. --- ## 5. The escape hatch: `onOpenTaskWindow` ```js onOpenTaskWindow(task) { if (!task) return this.selectedTaskId = task.id this.$chats.setActiveChat(task) } ``` Chain: `chats.setActiveChat` → `ui.openChat` → `openApp({ appKey: 'chat', payload: { chat } })` → `router/navigate.js#openApp`: - **Desktop mode** (route name `codx-junior-split`) → `ui.showApp` with `desktopKey: chat-` → a **new dockview panel** next to the board (de-duplicated by chat id, so re-opening focuses it). - **Single / mobile mode** → `$router.push({ name: 'chat', params: { chatId, chatName } })` → the chat replaces the screen. Note that on desktop this **does not close the inline pane** — you end up with the same chat in two places. Intentional (compare side-by-side / run long) but a known UX seam; Ctrl/Cmd+click on a card takes the same path. Clearing is handled defensively: ```js closeSideTask() { this.sideTaskId = null } // and activeBoardId() { this.sideTaskId = null } // switching boards invalidates the pane ``` --- ## 6. Why the Wall *doesn't* do this Worth stating explicitly, since the board-wall feature is nearby: ```js openBoardWall() { this.$storex.ui.openApp({ appKey: 'activity', payload: { board: this.activeBoardId, project: this.project || this.$projects.activeProject } }) } ``` The wall always opens the **Activity app** (panel on desktop, `/activity` route in single mode), and `Wall.vue#setActiveChat` calls `$chats.setActiveChat(chat)` → global panel/route.
